title: Research
text: Working papers and policy writing on carbon pricing, fiscal policy, and climate finance. Papers are available on request — please get in touch via the contact page.

title: Research
text:
Carbon Pricing

Total Effective Carbon Price (TECP): A Framework
Working paper, 2026
A framework for measuring the total effective carbon price across direct and indirect policy instruments — combining explicit carbon prices (taxes, ETS), implicit prices (fuel excises, fossil fuel subsidies), and the carbon-equivalent value of non-price instruments. The framework provides a comparable metric for assessing the stringency of climate policy across countries with heterogeneous instrument mixes.
Available on request.


A Carbon Consumption Tax for the EU
Working paper, 2026
On the design and political economy of a consumption-side carbon tax as a complement to the EU ETS and CBAM. The paper develops the rationale for taxing embedded carbon at the point of final consumption, the interaction with existing carbon pricing instruments, and the distributional and trade implications of consumption-based carbon taxation.
Available on request.

title: Research
text:
Green Growth

Green Structural Transformation Policy (GSTP) Framework
Working paper, 2026
A diagnostic framework for green structural transformation in developing economies. The paper sets out the analytical architecture for identifying green growth opportunities, sequencing reforms, and aligning industrial, fiscal, and climate policy in middle- and low-income country contexts.
Available on request.


Green Growth Policy — Lite (GGP-Lite)
Working paper, 2026
A streamlined diagnostic toolkit for green growth analysis, designed for application in country engagements with limited time and data. GGP-Lite distills the core analytical content of broader green growth diagnostics into a tractable applied tool.
Available on request.

title: Research
text:
Climate Finance & Fiscal Policy

Operationalizing Sustainability-Linked Lending
Working paper, 2026
On the design and operational architecture of sustainability-linked sovereign lending — including the selection of key performance indicators, the calibration of step-ups and step-downs, verification arrangements, and the broader institutional conditions under which sustainability-linked instruments can credibly shift sovereign behavior.
Available on request.

title: About
text: I am an economist working on climate, fiscal policy, and finance. My research focuses on the design of effective carbon pricing instruments, green growth diagnostics, and the fiscal and financial architecture of climate transitions.

title: About
text:
Background
I hold master’s degrees in philosophy, economics, and physics. My current work at the World Bank covers carbon pricing policy design, sustainability-linked sovereign lending, and country-level fiscal and climate policy engagements across Europe, Africa, and Asia.

title: About
text:
Research Interests
My work sits at the intersection of climate, fiscal, and financial policy:

Effective carbon pricing — measuring the total effective carbon price across direct and indirect policy instruments
Green growth diagnostics — frameworks for green structural transformation in developing economies
Sustainability-linked finance — the operational architecture of sustainability-linked sovereign lending
Fiscal policy for climate — carbon consumption taxes, border adjustments, and the political economy of climate fiscal reform

Alongside the technical work, I write on institutional economics, cooperative system design, and the philosophy of policy — drawing on game theory, Indian and Western philosophy, and the broader question of how durable collective arrangements emerge and sustain themselves.

title: About
